newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Gamesa buys around 90 T of Idaho wheat.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Gamesa buys around 90 T of Idaho wheat.

text.p: Mexican cookie maker Gamesa SA has agreed to buy around 90 tonnes of wheat from an Idaho-based grains company, the deputy governor of the state said Friday.
Butch Otter told Reuters that Jefferson Grain and Feed has clinched the deal with the closely-held Mexican company. He detailed the shipment as 50 train car loads of 3,500 bushels.

Otter was leading a Idaho trade mission and visting this northern industrial city where Gamesa is headquartered. "I would see it being sent in the next couple of months. When they need it we will get it to them," Otter added.
"The price of U.S. wheat is around $3.60 a bushel and I imagine that's what they got it for," Otter said, after being questioned on price.
Otter said he believed it would the first of many wheat contracts between Idaho and Mexico because of the stable business climate in Mexico.
Trade delegations from the U.S. states of Missouri and Colorado are also in Monterrey drumming up business and making contacts. They first visited Mexico City and and western city of Guadalajara.
